description: The plot titled “Hidden State Mean” illustrates how the absolute mean of hidden states varies across model layers for three series. The x-axis is labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale, and spans integer layers from 0 to 23 with tick labels shown at 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20. The y-axis is labeled “Abs Mean,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0 up to a little above 4 (with labeled ticks at 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4). One line is a blue dashed curve (no markers) labeled “hidden state mean before gate, avg 0.71,” which starts near 0.05 at layer 0, stays around roughly 0.2–0.5 through about layers 1–18, rises to about 0.9 around layer 19, jumps to about 2.6 around layer 21, and ends near 4.4 at layer 23. A second line is an orange dotted curve (no markers) labeled “hidden state mean after gate, avg 0.05,” which stays close to 0 across early layers and gradually increases, reaching around 0.1 by the final layers, with a small dip visible around layer 22 before returning near ~0.1 at layer 23. The third line is a green solid curve (no markers) labeled “hidden state …” (the remainder of the label is obscured), which also remains near 0 at early layers and increases gradually across layers, ending around ~0.1 at layer 23.
